# nexus operation get

List operations, or with ID, get one operation

Without ID: Lists operations newest first, limited to providers whose read scope the caller holds. Read-only. Paged with limit and cursor; filter by status, provider, createdAfter and createdBefore.

With ID: Returns one operation with its status, timestamps, result and structured error. Read-only. Requires the read scope of the operation's provider.

## Usage

```
nexus operation get [ID] [flags]
```

## Examples

```
  # List operations
  nexus operation get
  # Get one operation
  nexus operation get <id>
```

## Flags

```
      --cursor string        Opaque cursor from a previous page's nextCursor.
      --filter stringArray   key=value, repeatable: print only objects whose dot path has this value; a repeated key matches any of its values; the host filters by status, provider, createdAfter, createdBefore
  -h, --help                 help for get
      --limit int            Page size: default 100, maximum 1000.
  -o, --output string        output format: table, json, jsonl, yaml (default table on a terminal, jsonl otherwise)
      --select strings       print only these dot paths of each object, comma-separated, such as name,properties.state; host and id are always kept
      --stdin                read JSON Lines objects from stdin, such as another command's output, and run once per line: each binds its host and its id or id; a line without host uses the target host
      --stop-on-error        with --stdin, stop at the first line that fails
      --tag strings          target every configured host with this tag; comma-separated or repeated for any of several
```

## Global flags

```
      --host string   target hosts: configured names, comma-separated, or all (default: NEXUS_HOST, then the default host)
      --verbose       log each request and response status to stderr
```
